zh: 按位置计数意味着每个下标区间单独算，内容相同也不去重。每个回文都有唯一的中心：长度为奇数的中心在某个字符上，长度为偶数的中心在两个字符之间。若某中心能向两侧扩展的最大半径是 k，那么它恰好贡献 k 个回文，所以答案就是所有中心最大半径之和。注意总数可达约 5.6×10^14，要用 64 位整数。
逐个中心暴力扩展是 O(n²)，而字符串可长达 3355 万。用 Manacher 算法：维护目前右端最远的回文区间 [l, r]；新中心 i 落在区间内时，它关于区间中心的镜像位置的半径（截断到 r−i+1 为止）可以直接作为起点，再只对边界外的字符继续比较。r 只会单调右移，所以总时间 O(n)。奇数和偶数中心分两趟各做一次。

读一行字符串（忽略行尾的 \r）。奇数趟：k 初值为 i>r 时取 1，否则 min(radius[l+r−i], r−i+1)；当 s[i−k]==s[i+k] 时 k++；记 radius[i]=k、累加 k，若 i+k−1>r 则 l=i−k+1、r=i+k−1。偶数趟：k 初值为 i>r 时取 0，否则 min(radius[l+r−i+1], r−i+1)；比较 s[i−k−1] 与 s[i+k]；累加 k，越界时 l=i−k、r=i+k−1。两趟复用同一个半径数组以节省内存，最后输出总和；空串输出 0。
en: Counting by position means every index range counts separately, even when the contents repeat. Every palindrome has a unique center: for odd length it sits on a character, for even length it sits between two characters. If the largest radius a center can expand to on both sides is k, that center contributes exactly k palindromes, so the answer is the sum of the maximum radii over all centers. The total can reach about 5.6×10^14, so use 64-bit integers.

Expanding each center by brute force is O(n²), while the string can be about 33.5 million characters long. Use Manacher's algorithm: keep the palindrome interval [l, r] that reaches farthest to the right so far; when a new center i lies inside it, the radius of its mirror position about that interval's center (capped at r−i+1) is a valid starting point, and only characters beyond the boundary need to be compared. r only moves right, so the total time is O(n). Do one pass for odd centers and one pass for even centers.

Read one line (ignore a trailing \r). Odd pass: start k at 1 if i>r, otherwise at min(radius[l+r−i], r−i+1); while s[i−k]==s[i+k], increment k; store radius[i]=k, add k to the answer, and if i+k−1>r set l=i−k+1 and r=i+k−1. Even pass: start k at 0 if i>r, otherwise at min(radius[l+r−i+1], r−i+1); compare s[i−k−1] with s[i+k]; add k, and when it passes the boundary set l=i−k and r=i+k−1. Reuse the same radius array for both passes to save memory, then print the total; the empty string gives 0.

explanationEn:
## The original counting object and correcting a curation misreading

fastprep/Pure Storage/purestorage-count-different-palindrome-substrings.md at the fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc explicitly gives ll,ll as an example and writes "two distinct substrings that only happen to be equal". So "different ways to pick" are distinguished by index range, and substrings must not be deduplicated by content. Every non-empty contiguous substring that reads the same forwards and backwards counts once; the same content occurring at different positions is counted separately.

The original example hellolle has 8 single characters, 2 ll, lol, lloll and ellolle, 13 in total; deduplicating by content would give only 8. wowpurerocks has 12 single characters, plus wow and rer, 14 in total; deduplicating by content would give only 11. Both original answers are correct and are kept in full; the so-called conflict only arose because the old blocking reason misread position counting as content deduplication. The upper/lower case illustration in the original definition does not change the function's explicit input range of only lowercase letters.

The original constraints section is a placeholder with no bound on the string length. This site neither borrows its own length limit from another problem of the same company nor fabricates original limits such as n≤200000; it supports every lowercase string within the existing 32MiB per-case text input budget. The input is one line s, and the trailing newline may be omitted, so without a newline the length can reach 33554432. An empty line denotes the empty string, and returning 0 is this site's publicly stated mathematical extension. The original Java int return type cannot hold the full count, so this site outputs the exact mathematical integer without a modulus, using 64 bits; over the full transmissible domain the upper bound n(n+1)/2≤562949970198528 is below 2^50.

## Approach

For every character center, compute the radius of odd-length palindromes, and for every gap between characters, compute the radius of even-length palindromes. An odd radius k covers k non-empty palindromes around that center, and an even radius k also corresponds to k non-empty palindromes, so the answer is the sum of all odd and even radii.

Use Manacher's algorithm to maintain the current rightmost palindrome interval [l,r]. When the center lies inside the interval, we can borrow the known radius of the position symmetric to it about the interval's center, truncated at the right boundary; then we only keep comparing and expanding beyond the boundary, where nothing is known. The odd and even cases are scanned separately, and the two passes reuse the same int radius array; we neither build a transformed string of length 2n with separators nor keep two radius arrays at the same time.

## Proof of correctness

Every non-empty palindrome has a unique odd or even center, and its length is uniquely determined by the center and the radius. When the maximum radius of a center is k, every radius of the same parity from 1 to k gives a palindrome and no larger one does, so that center contributes exactly k; summing over all centers neither misses nor double counts any index range.

The known interval [l,r] is a palindrome, so characters inside it that are symmetric about its center are equal. If the current center satisfies i≤r, the part of the mirrored center's radius that does not cross the interval boundary can be transferred directly to i; if the full mirrored radius ends inside the boundary, the unequal characters that stop it from expanding further also lie inside the interval and remain unequal after mirroring. If the mirrored radius touches the boundary, only the part up to the boundary is guaranteed, and expansion continues by comparing the actual characters. So initialization plus expansion yields the current maximum radius. If expansion goes beyond the known rightmost boundary, [l,r] is updated, which preserves the invariant; by induction over the centers from left to right, all radii of both passes are correct, and their sum is the answer.

## Complexity and full-domain memory

In each pass, the part determined directly by the mirror is never expanded again; every successful comparison beyond the boundary advances r, r advances at most n times, and each center has only a constant number of additional failed comparisons, so the total time of both passes is O(n). The extra radius array takes 4n bytes and the string O(n); no 2n transformed string is used. At the maximum n=32MiB the array takes 128MiB, and the string with its possible reserved capacity can still run within the native 256MiB limit; this must be verified with the actual memory recorded on the largest input, rather than claiming that every language uses the same memory. The package allows 3 seconds, 256MiB and 64KiB of output; local measurements are not Linux sandbox evidence.

## Independent verification

The small oracle truly enumerates every non-empty interval and checks whether that substring equals its reverse, without computing center radii. The native reference is actually run on 163 unique inputs (3 public/supplementary ones and 160 other boundary and random inputs); in addition, all 1093 strings of length 0..6 over the alphabet abc are enumerated exhaustively and checked against direct enumeration and an independent palindromic tree.

The palindromic tree creates one node per distinct palindrome content, but each time a character is appended it counts all palindrome occurrences ending at the current position by the number of palindrome nodes on the suffix-link chain, and then sums over all positions, so the oracle still counts by position rather than counting deduplicated nodes. Medium and large random strings and periodic strings get their expected outputs from this different algorithm. The two largest inputs are all a's (every interval, n(n+1)/2) and alternating ab (exactly all odd-length intervals, floor((n+1)²/4)), checked with independent closed forms.

Three linear negative controls respectively miss even palindromes, miss single characters and overflow 32 bits; kills are explicitly not faked by letting a naive deduplicating set algorithm time out on the largest input. The original examples already distinguish position counting from content deduplication directly. All official negative controls must exit normally to count as valid rejections.
